page: Amazon Web Services m9gd.24xlarge is a general-purpose, Nitro-based instance powered by AWS ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 architecture. The instance provides 96 dedicated physical cores running at 3.3 GHz with a single thread per core, eliminating hyperthreading contention. It is configured with 384 GB of system memory, matching a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. For localized I/O, the instance bundles 5,700 GB of NVMe SSD instance storage and delivers a 50 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. It contains no dedicated GPU hardware accelerators.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional multi-threaded performance. The 96-core configuration achieves top-tier results in multi-core stress-ng workloads, Geekbench multi-core tests, Clang compilation, and decompression. Memory subsystem performance is similarly high, with top-tier cached and uncached read bandwidth, as well as high-throughput Redis set operations exceeding 268 million operations per second. CPU encryption and single-core stress-ng tests perform in the middle percentile, but general single-core Geekbench metrics remain competitive.

The integration of substantial high-speed local NVMe storage combined with high memory bandwidth offers efficient resource utilization for data-intensive applications. Because the instance provides dedicated physical ARM cores and integrated storage without requiring supplemental block volumes for temporary files, it provides strong architectural efficiency for sustained parallel execution.

Workloads best aligned with the m9gd.24xlarge include large-scale distributed databases, in-memory caching systems such as Redis, high-throughput static web serving, software build clusters, and data processing pipelines requiring high local disk capacity.
description: Amazon Web Services m9gd.24xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by 96 dedicated ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 physical cores clocked at 3.3 GHz. Configured with 384 GB of system memory, 5,700 GB of bundled NVMe SSD local instance storage, and a 50 Gbps baseline network interface, it provides a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio without hyperthreading overhead. Benchmark testing shows top-tier throughput in multi-core compute, software compilation, database transactions, and in-memory key-value operations, paired with high memory read bandwidth. Although it lacks discrete GPU acceleration, its dense compute and bundled NVMe capacity deliver high resource efficiency for demanding multi-threaded tasks. The m9gd.24xlarge is well suited for enterprise database deployments, caching layers, continuous integration pipelines, and large-scale web service infrastructure.
